title: Stable filtered cycle quotients and transported cohomology image filtration
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], $K$ an integer-indexed cochain complex, and $L$ a decreasing filtration by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration]. Assume that for every degree $n$ there are integers $\ell_n,h_n$ such that $L^{\ell_n}K^n=K^n$ and $L^{h_n}K^n=0$, using the image steps [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Given objects $Y^n$ and isomorphisms $c_n:H^n(K)\cong Y^n$, there is a finite decreasing filtration $H$ on every $Y^n$ with $H^pY^n=(c_n)_*\operatorname{im}(H^n(L^pK)\to H^n(K))$. For every $p,n$ there exists $t\ge1$ such that for every $r\ge t$ the inclusion $B_r^{p,n}\subseteq Z_r^{p,n}$ holds and its cokernel is isomorphic to $\operatorname{gr}^pH(Y^n)$. Here $Z_r,B_r$ are the filtered cycle/boundary subobjects of [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients].

proof.text: For each n define the p-th step on H^n(K) to be the image of H^n(L^pK) → H^n(K). The factorization through L^pK of the inclusion of L^qK for p ≤ q gives antitonicity. Pick bounds for degrees n-1,n,n+1. For p below all their lower bounds the subcomplex inclusion is an isomorphism in these three degrees, so its homology image is top. Above the upper bound in degree n its homology image is zero. Thus the image filtration is finite. Fix p,n. Choose t ≥ 1 so that L^(p+t)K^(n+1)=0 and L^(p-t+1)K^(n-1)=K^(n-1). Antitonicity keeps these equalities true for every r ≥ t. In the formulas for Z_r and B_r the outer steps can therefore be replaced by zero and the whole object. The cycles are the images in gr^pK^n of actual cycles in L^pK^n, while the boundaries are the images of actual boundaries of K intersected with L^pK^n. The abelian subquotient isomorphism identifies Z_r/B_r with the quotient of the image of H^n(L^pK) by the image of H^n(L^(p+1)K). This is the graded piece of the image filtration. For a family c_n:H^n(K) ≅ Y^n, take direct images of these steps along c_n.hom. Their antitonicity is preserved by the direct-image functor. Since each c_n is an isomorphism, direct image preserves top and bottom and identifies the successive inclusion arrows up to isomorphism. Applying the cokernel functor to these squares gives the graded-piece comparisons. This yields the exact step formula, finiteness and stationary-quotient isomorphisms below.

theorem degreewiseFiltered_stable_quotient
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C]
    (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (L : DecreasingFiltration K)
    (hfinite : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ lo hi : ℤ,
      L.complexStep lo n = ⊤ ∧ L.complexStep hi n = ⊥)
    (Y : ℤ → C) (c : ∀ n : ℤ, K.homology n ≅ Y n) :
    ∃ H : ∀ n : ℤ, DecreasingFiltration (Y n),
      (∀ n : ℤ, (H n).IsFinite) ∧
      (∀ p n : ℤ, (H n).step p =
        (Subobject.«exists» (c n).hom).obj
          (imageSubobject (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (L.step p).arrow n))) ∧
      (∀ p n : ℤ, ∃ (t : ℤ) (ht : 1 ≤ t), ∀ (r : ℤ) (hr : t ≤ r),
        ∃ hBZ : L.complexBoundaries p n r ≤ L.complexCycles p n r,
          Nonempty (cokernel (Subobject.ofLE _ _ hBZ) ≅ (H n).gradedPiece p))
